analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md: it adds one troubleshooting bullet (head lines 581-588) for re-pairing while cluster services run. It says each service answers with the new pairing within seconds, logs `this Mac's pairing changed`, and that a Mac still refusing with `refused (handshakeRejected)` needs `darkbloom cluster stop` then `darkbloom cluster`. No code, protocol, key custody, attestation or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

Security review: the guidance tells operators to restart a stale service rather than weaken pairing, disable encryption or relax a handshake check. It prescribes no plaintext fallback, so it does not touch the encrypted paired-link contract at lines 281-283 or the cable-copy controls at lines 292-301. The new text does not alter the trust model for provider-to-provider cluster links, and the retained prefix-cache threat (T-041) is not affected. The log path `~/.darkbloom/cluster-setup/service.log` was already documented in base at lines 528 and 554, so no new disclosure is introduced. The log message names no secrets.

Unverified contract: the doc claims services pick up the new pairing within seconds via a linked architecture section (`cluster-service-listeners-follow-the-cable-and-the-pairing`), and that a service started by an earlier release keeps the old pairing. The implementation that makes a running service rebind to a new pairing is not in this batch. The next pass should confirm that this listener refresh does not accept a stale or unauthenticated pairing, does not leave an old pairing's keys or prompt-cache records usable (cf. the `--forget` cleanup at base lines 603-606), and that the SAS/code confirmation still gates a new pairing. No finding is raised, because the supplied evidence is documentation only and no regression is shown.
